name: Grass blade
notes:
ONE blade — the member a clump and a haystack are both piles of. Robin, 2026-08-10: *"a clump of grass should be an assembly of multiple 'grass blade' assemblies. A haystack is then a pile of 'grass blades' with the 'dry' properties."*

NOTHING NEW IS DECLARED. These are the grass clump's own numbers, lifted out of it: leaf area LAI 3.0 x pi(0.06)^2 over 32 blades of length 0.35 m fixes the width at 3.03 mm, which sits inside the measured 2-3 mm of Lolium perenne. The clump is now 32 of THESE rather than 32 slabs it described itself, and its mass is unchanged because the matter is.

A DRY blade is the same geometry made of `straw` — that is what a haystack is a pile of, and it is why the material is a property of the blade rather than of the pile.

★★★ 2026-08-17 — THE BLADE IS A LAMINA PLUS A MIDRIB, AND THAT IS GEOMETRY, NOT A SHAPE FACTOR (docs/46 row 64). Robin: *"Render can fudge, physics shouldn't."* Its stiffness was about to be modelled as flat_slab x 2.0, with the 2.0 bounded by measurement but not itself measured — a fudge-shaped patch over a geometry this file can simply state. Declared instead: two lamina wings either side of a thicker median band. The MEASURED input is the thickness ratio, Imperata cylindrica midrib 429.66 +/- 41.32 um against lamina 196.47 +/- 14.33 um = 2.187 (Sima et al. 2018); the stiffness recruitment is then a RESULT, I/I_flat = 1.946, which `Assembly::section` computes by the parallel-axis theorem and a test cross-checks against the closed form (1-f) + f*r^3. It lands inside the 1.5-2.4 that two independent routes gave, without anyone choosing it. ★ THE ONE UNMEASURED INPUT IS NOW THE MIDRIB'S WIDTH FRACTION (0.10) — which is progress rather than a fix: a midrib width is a physical dimension somebody can go and measure, whereas a shape factor is a knob. Source it and this file has no free parameter left. ★ MATTER RISES 11.9% against the uniform slab, which is correct: a blade thickened at its midrib holds more substance than a flat one of the same envelope. Leaf AREA is unchanged, so the LAI derivation above still holds. ★ NOT EXPRESSIBLE YET: a V-FOLD. Ellis (1976) classifies Poaceae blades by the angle between the two lamina arms, and `Part` carries `along` (a direction) but no ROLL about it, so folded arms cannot be declared. That is a real gap in `Part`, and the same one docs/46 row 30 names for grain direction.
